directions.name: E — Story garden
directions.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Generate an ORIGINAL illustration brand-direction board for Hey Kahani, a children's storytelling brand, intended for website illustration and decorative vectors. Use the supplied image solely as a STYLE REFERENCE, not an edit target: invent new assets and compositions, do not reproduce its exact artwork, website text, brand identity or arrangement. This is a fresh exploratory direction, not a variation of previous kite/book/leaf/sun grids. Avoid the previous layout of six icons above a cream website strip. NO text, labels, typography, watermarks, logo, product hardware, website screenshot or photographic mockups. Landscape art board with confident intentional composition. Render illustration only. No glossy 3D, realistic lighting, drop shadows, stock clipart look or airbrushed gradients. Use Hey Kahani's palette, adapting the reference rather than copying its colours blindly: Gulab Red #D3000A, Kesar Sand #FFF1D6, Sky Blue #63C3FE, Mango Yellow #FECB74, Story Ink #05334A. Supporting Parrot Green #2B9863, Marigold Orange #FF5D27, Lavender tea #D6C9E4, small accents of Hibiscus Pink #EF2289 or Rangoli Violet #B558DD. Primary colours anchor the overall system; accent colours are sparse.
REFERENCE-LED DIRECTION E: contemporary naive Indian botanical and animal illustration inspired by the reference's detailed tiger, delicate plants, spice pods and hand-painted decorative objects. A richly distinctive MINIATURE NATURAL WORLD, not simplified blobs or chunky stamp icons. Illustrate a long gently curving orange tiger stretched across the lower centre beneath a whimsical banyan sprig; oversized mango leaves in the upper left, a small saffron flower and three cardamom seedpods upper right, an elegant Indian roller bird perched on a curling stem on the left, and a tiny flowering vine on the right. Use uneven hand-drawn outlines selectively, angular naive anatomy, decorative internal vein marks, individually drawn stripes, stippled seed details and gentle brush-like irregularities inside flat opaque shapes. These details give artisanal richness but remain sparse and readable. Mostly white/Kesar paper-white negative space, artwork occupies about half the canvas, a few isolated botanical assets clearly spaced apart around the larger tiger/tree vignette. Flat vivid but sophisticated spot colours. Animals can have tiny natural eyes; no anthropomorphic smiling plants. South Asian specificity from real flora/fauna and decorative drawing craft. A gentle contemporary folk illustration language with care and personality, clearly much more descriptive and intricate than organic icon shapes. NO sun, kite or open book. NO fake torn paper texture, no rubber stamp distress.

REFERENCE-LED DIRECTION F: bold conceptual editorial illustration from the geometric character/world approach in the reference. Create FOUR LARGE ART TILES in a 2x2 arrangement with narrow cream gutters; each tile uses a different full-bleed flat colour ground: sky blue, mango yellow, Story Ink, and Kesar Sand. Confident giant abstract masses, extreme cropping, playful unexpected scale, spare one- or two-stroke expressions on selected forms, surreal but meaningful metaphor. Original subjects: top left a big red arch enclosing a tiny yellow listening shell with long blue sound ribbons; top right an oversized pair of green pea-pod shapes that open to release a tiny orange sailboat; bottom left a lavender dream-cloud with a tiny red ladder and yellow crescent in a dark blue night; bottom right a stack of giant wonky blue and red balancing pebbles supporting a minuscule orange flower. Large simple curved and angular geometry, clipped corners, no thin descriptive outlines, almost no texture, no botanical detailing. Gentle tiny facial expressions may appear on the cloud and one pebble, fewer than half the forms. Original visual metaphors for imagination, listening, rest and discovery rather than literal benefit icons. Strong contrast, bold cropped composition, playful relationships and strange scale. This direction must feel like colourful conceptual illustration scenes rather than a sheet of isolated icons. No orange smiling Headspace logo circle and no copies of the reference scenes.

REFERENCE-LED DIRECTION G: graphic playroom animal vocabulary, toy-like geometric creatures with visible modular construction, simple flat patterns and tiny bright eyes. Create a white landscape specimen sheet with SIX INVENTED ANIMAL ASSETS spaced generously, different sizes and playful orientations: a plump Indian roller bird with broad blue wings and little red feet, a curved elephant with oversized round ear and short raised trunk, a winding fish with fan tail and three broad patterned scales, a butterfly built from asymmetric petal wings and striped body, a squat frog with one long folded leg, and a spiral-shell snail perched on a tiny uneven block. Do not copy the specific animals or silhouettes from the reference. Animals made from clean simple thick geometric primitives: circles, discs, half circles, rounded rectangles, bold wedges. REFERENCE-LED DIRECTION H: nonfigurative expressive gesture system, like the reference's freeform squiggles, open loops, irregular starbursts and blobs. ZERO recognisable objects, animals, people, books, kites, plants, suns or faces. Create a fresh landscape illustration toolkit composition on an almost white Kesar-tinted canvas. Composition is asymmetrical and spacious with 10-12 highly different abstract graphic marks: one large hand-drawn red looping line with a thick/thin pressure change, a sky-blue scalloped puddle, a mango-yellow irregular donut with a lopsided opening, one dark-ink open starburst outline, a springy green zigzag with rounded elbows, an orange bent capsule, a pair of overlapping lavender and sky blue pebble shapes, a small red wavy arch, a broad yellow undulating ribbon, and one tiny pink torn-looking oval accent. Giant forms gently crop into two corners; smaller complete isolated shapes are clearly spaced away from them. Emphasise beautiful offbeat contours, unexpected negative-space cutouts, gestural motion frozen in shape, lively artistic composition and interesting silhouette. Mix filled masses with bold open line marks, no shadow, no texture, no outline around filled forms. Deliberately handmade vector-friendly drawing with raw spontaneous confident energy. Never perfect circles, uniform blob confetti, conventional corporate Memphis pattern or repetitive sprinkles. Leave a large calm central pocket where a website heading could live, but add no actual heading or grey placeholder text.
